docs.title: Panasonic Microwave Disable Door Lock
docs.text:
To disable the automatic electronic door lock on most Panasonic microwave models, press Turbo Defrost (or Auto Defrost), followed immediately by Timer/Clock (or Timer), and then Popcorn in sequence.

A long beep and the display showing OFF indicate the lock is deactivated; repeating this sequence reactivates it.

  2. Unsalted butter
  3. Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

docs.title: Directions
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
  2. Wash the potatoes and place them directly on the oven baking rack. Bake for 45 to 60 minutes, until very tender when pierced with a skewer.
  3. When the potatoes are done, cut them down the middle and squeeze both ends. Place a slice of butter in the middle of the potato, sprinkle with salt and pepper and serve hot.

docs.title: Classic Pancakes Recipe
docs.text: Ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour 2 tablespoons granulated sugar 2 teaspoons baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 3/4 cup milk 1 large egg 2 tablespoons melted butter (plus more for cooking) 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

docs.title: Instructions:
docs.text:
1. Combine Dry Ingredients: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
  2. Mix Wet Ingredients: In another bowl, whisk together the milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla extract.
  3. Combine Wet and Dry: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. The batter should be a bit lumpy—don't overmix!
  4. Cook Pancakes: Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat. Lightly grease with butter. Pour about 1/4 cup of batter onto the skillet for each pancake. Cook until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set, then flip and cook until golden brown on the other side.
  5. Serve: Serve warm with your favorite toppings like maple syrup, fresh fruit, whipped cream, or chocolate chips.

docs.title: Optional:
docs.text: Add blueberries: 1. Once you've poured the batter onto the skillet (about 1/4 cup for each pancake), sprinkle a few blueberries on top of each pancake. This way, the blueberries will be evenly distributed in each pancake. 2. Cook as usual until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set, then flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes, until golden brown.

docs.title: Shokupan -- Japanese Milk Bread Loaf -- 日式生吐司
docs.text:
Try: for 450g loaf pan (7 Bread Flour 230g Yudane(湯種) 105g .5&.5 Milk 150ml Sugar(+Honey) 25g Yeast 4g Egg 1 (25g) Salt 2g Butter 20g

====================================================== 很多人不知道什么是生吐司?其实生吐司就是指不用加任何东西单吃就很好吃的吐司，说也可以说原味吐司，我们现在推荐给大家量一款适合在家庭制作的日式生吐司的做法，操作比较简单易上手。

日式生吐司原版配方材料明细： 1. Bread Flour=高筋面粉250g、Sugar=糖25g、Salt=盐5g、Yeast=酵母3g、Milk=鲜奶175g、Cream=鲜奶油25g、Butter无盐奶油20g、Eggs=全蛋25g 2. Bread Flour 1000g, Sugar 100g, Cream 100g, water 620g, Salt 15g, Honey 20g Butter 80g 3. 高筋面粉500g、砂糖50g、盐10g、速发酵母6g、鲜奶350g、动物性鲜奶油50g、鸡蛋50g、无盐奶油40g

100%中种法北海道吐司: 1、今天的北海道吐司就用了100%中种法。此分量是2个450克吐司模的量。首先将中种原料：高粉500g、酵母3g、淡奶油150g、牛奶160g、蛋白35g、细砂糖15g，揉成团，放保鲜盒或盖保鲜膜室温下发酵至2.5倍大。可以提前一晚揉个中种放冰箱冷藏发酵17小时以上，成品的口感会更好。 2、发好的中种面团很容易就能撕成小块，再与主面团原料混合，-主面团的原料：蛋白40g、酵母2g、细砂糖75g、奶粉30g、盐6g一起揉至较光滑。 3、再加入黄油20g继续揉至完出筋完全状态，这里的面团能用手撑开而不破。然后发酵半小时左右. 4、分割成6等份，擀开，对折，竖过来擀成牛舍状. 5、放吐司盒里发酵至九分满， 6、放预热好的烤箱中下层，上下火185度，烤35分钟，记得上色后加盖锡纸啊，要不糊了顶就不好看了。还有一点各家烤箱的温度都不太一样，一定要掌握好自己烤箱的脾气 ，适当调整时间。

湯種法換算??? 若是要將其它麵包改成湯種麵包。 把乾溼料的20%計算出來。即為所需要的湯種重量~ 例如，主麵糰所有材料加起來是600g (麵粉、液體、雞蛋、酵母、糖、鹽巴等等~) 20% 即為120g，根據比例1:5 即為麵粉20g 水100g 再往回扣除主麵糰中的麵粉20g，液體100g，即為妳剩下麵粉 以及液體需要的量~ ==========================================

docs.text:
[材料] 帶蓋吐司一條 12兩 高筋麵粉 270g 鹽巴 3g 砂糖 15g 蜂蜜 25g 速發酵母 3g 冰牛奶 80ml 動物性鮮奶油 80ml 冰水 50ml 無鹽奶油 25g (軟化備用)

湯種牛奶吐司 (https://yummymum.tw/tongzhongmilkbread/) [材料]1條土司份量 20X10X6公分模具 (7.87"x3.94"x2.36") 高筋麵粉 20g 水 100g 高筋麵粉 280g 細砂糖 40g 雞蛋 1顆 (25g) 鮮奶 90ml 無鹽奶油 30g 酵母 5g 鹽巴 5g ======================================== 食材明细 高筋面粉500g、砂糖50g、盐10g、速发酵母6g、鲜奶350g、动物性鲜奶油50g、鸡蛋50g、无盐奶油40g

日式鲜奶生吐司的做法： 1.把所有面粉和砂糖一起倒入盆中，混合后稍稍搅拌一下. 2.把动物性鲜奶油g、鸡蛋50g、无盐奶油倒入盆中 3、搅拌机低速3分钟，然后开中速10分钟(打至光滑)，然后倒入奶油 4.继续以低速2分钟+中速4分钟(打至面团表面光滑) 5. 放好基本发酵60分钟左右. 6、然后把面团分割成允250g/个小面团，继续松弛20分钟 7、拿一颗面团，用手多奢一下，排除里面的空气 8、然后翻面，折三折 9、四个面团一样的步骤，休息5分钟 10、直接杆开成长椭圆 11、翻面，光滑面朝下，靠近自己这端压薄，卷起 12、收口面朝下，放入吐司模 13、最后发酵 50分 (发到吐司模9分满) 14、上火170度/下火220度烘烤35分钟 (25分钟后转向，若上色太重，关上火) 15、这是切片后，隔天在进烤箱酥烤后的，层次依然明显。

生吐司：（顏色可自行調整）這裡使用加蓋上火210下火210烘烤32分鐘 重量為12兩吐司

高筋麵粉280克 細砂糖40克 牛奶215克 鹽巴4克 酵母3克 無鹽奶油20克

作法： 1.將麵粉及牛奶,砂糖 低速攪拌進行水合法30分鐘 2.加入酵母及鹽巴（分開位置擺放,可放麵團的兩側） 3.使用6速攪打2分鐘,停一次再繼續攪打,總共約攪打12分鐘 4.等待薄膜出現後可加入軟化的無鹽奶油進行最後一次的攪打,打至薄膜產生即可進行分割 5.分割後的麵團非常柔軟 若發現麵團不夠柔軟時可能是攪打不足或者麵團需要休息3~5分鐘再進行分割 6.分成四等份平均一份約130~140克,簡單桿開後對折,做完全部麵團後再從第一個麵團開始桿成長條狀,捲起 7.捲起後放入吐司模具中進行發酵約1.5小時內(由於沒有基本發酵剛出爐的吐司很綿密有彈性) 8.發至八分九分滿的吐司蓋上蓋子進行烘烤32分鐘 9.出爐後輕敲,立即倒出吐司,等待放涼後可以切片,常溫三日都還是很綿密唷！

=====================================================

docs.title: Original Recipe
docs.text:
https://mr-cheesecake.com/blogs/news/no19_english

cream cheese 200g granulated sugar 100g sour cream 180g Greek yogurt 50g cream 100g white chocolate 50g egg yolk 2 pieces lemon juice 9g vanilla 1/4 piece tonka beans 1/2 piece cornstarch 20g

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text: -Line a parchment paper in cake tin -Bring cream cheese and egg yolk to the room temperature -Beat egg yolk in advance -Cut white chocolate into small pieces -Grate tonka beans -Cut open vanilla beans and scrape out the seeds -Preheat the oven to 180℃

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: (1) Combine cream cheese and granulated sugar in the bowl, and mix in a hot-water bath until it has a smooth texture. (2) Combine sour cream and Greek yogurt in another bowl, and mix well using a rubber spatula. (3) Mix the 2 egg yolks and add into (2) above in thirds, mixing well with a whisk after each third is added. Add lemon juice and cornstarch and mix well. (4) Heat cream in a small pan on medium heat, add white chocolate, grated tonka beans, vanilla bean seeds and pods. Turn off the heat after bringing to a boil. (5) Mix (1) and (4) with a whisk. Add (3) and mix until it becomes smooth. Strain and pour into a cake tin lined with parchment paper. (6) Place the filled cake tin on a cooking sheet (at least 3 cm deep) and place into the oven. Pour 3 cm of water into the cooking sheet. (7) Bake at 180℃ for 25 min. and 150℃ for 20 min. Take out of the oven, allow it to cool, and turn the cheesecake out. Cool in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.

docs.title: 全麥麵包【湯種法】Tangzhong Wholemeal Toast
docs.text:
全麥麵包【湯種法】 Tangzhong Wholemeal Toast https://www.christinesrecipes.com/2012/10/tangzhong-wholemeal-toast.html

分量: 1條吐司麵包（麵包模大小 20.5cmx10.5cmx9.5cm） 材料: 牛奶 110克 全蛋液 45克 湯種 100克 糖 40克 鹽 5克 高筋麵粉（bread flour） 200克 全麥麵粉（wholemeal / whole wheat flour）150克 快速乾酵母（instant dry yeast） 6克 無鹽牛油（無鹽奶油，置室溫軟化）40克

做法: 把所有材料（除牛油外）依次倒進麵包機（先放濕的材料，然後放下乾的材料）：牛奶，蛋汁，湯種，糖，鹽，高筋和全麥麵粉，最後放酵母。 選擇麵包機的 dough功能，材料搞拌至成一麵團（見圖1），才放進已軟化的牛油，繼續搞拌，直至擴展階段即可。即拉開麵團成薄膜時破洞呈鋸齒狀。 當麵包機停機，等待麵團第一次發酵完畢，見麵團發大兩倍。就取出，放在清潔的工作台上，灑點高筋粉。 用手按壓麵團，擠出空氣。分割成三等份，滾圓（見圖2）。用保鮮膜蓋著，室溫靜置 15分鐘。 用擀麵棍把每個小麵團從中央向外滾成橢圓形。從上向下褶1/3後，壓緊（見圖3）。再從下往上褶1/3後，壓緊（見圖4）。收口朝下，把麵團上下壓長，約30cm（見圖5），翻面捲成圓柱形（見圖6及7）。收口朝下（見圖8），放入麵包模中進行最後發酵。發酵至8分滿（見圖9），蓋上麵包模蓋（如沒有麵包模蓋，可輕輕塗上少許全蛋液）。放入已預熱至170C / 335F的焗爐中，焗約30至35分鐘。取出放在鐵架上放涼，即成。

溫馨提示： 有關湯種的材料和做法請參考這湯種做法網誌，只須量出所需的分量即可。 加了全麥麵粉的麵團較難搞打至完全階段（即拉開薄膜破洞呈圓形）。切勿過度搞打麵團，以免溫度上升而變黏。只需打至夠筋性（即拉開薄膜破洞呈鋸齒狀），即可。

docs.title: 最常用的三种发面法
docs.text: 先说最常用的三种发面法：

docs.title: 直接法
docs.text: 这是最基本的面包的方法，指是将面团所需要材料搅拌好，再进行发酵制做。也就是说按照揉面团-----基础发酵-----排气分割松驰----整形入模再次发酵----烘烤的过程来操作。这样做出来的面包，操作相对简单，适合小餐包或者调理型面包。

docs.title: 中种法
docs.text: 中种法刚是预先发酵面团。一般将面团原料分为两部分，一是中种主面团，一部分是主面团。中种面团不需要揉出膜，只要成团就可以了。可在冰箱冷藏发酵17小时以上，也可以室温发酵至2-3倍大再与主面团混合 。一般的中种法分为70%中种法和100%中种法。中种法通过延长发酵过程会让成品面包的质地和味道都提升。有人说中种法太费时间了，个人却感觉只要合理安排好时间，中种法实际是更容易操作的。

docs.title: 汤种法
docs.text: 汤种法实际还是属于直接法的一种，只不过在加了汤种面糊。汤种面包和其他面包最大的差别在于淀粉糊化使吸水量增加了，因此面包的组织会柔软，有弹性而且可以延缓老化。

docs.title: 西湖牛肉羹(Westlakebeefsoup)
docs.text: 西湖牛肉羹是江南地区汉族传统名菜，属于杭帮菜。由于它香淳润滑、鲜美可口，常会 提前上席作为润喉开胃的羹汤。西湖牛肉羹也是深受普通老百姓喜爱的食品。仅用牛肉 、鸡蛋和香菇，便可做成价廉物美的羹汤

docs.title: 材料
docs.text: 牛肉 100克 平菇 50克 南豆腐 50克 鸡蛋白 1颗 香菜 2根 生姜 2片 香葱 1根

docs.title: 调味料
docs.text: 盐 1/2小匙 鸡精 1/4小匙 白胡椒粉 1/4小匙

docs.title: 水淀粉
docs.text: 玉米淀粉 1大匙 清水 2大匙

docs.title: 做法步骤
docs.text:
1. 牛肉剁碎，尽量剁的细碎一些
  2. 平菇去蒂切碎，南豆腐切小块，香菜切碎，香葱切碎，生姜切片
  3. 玉米淀粉+水调成水淀粉，鸡蛋分开蛋黄蛋清，只取蛋清备用。
  4. 锅内烧开一锅水，取一汤匙开水放入牛肉碗内，将牛肉化开，用漏匙将牛肉 沥干血水备用。
  5. 将平菇、南豆腐块、姜片放入水中煮开。
  6. 加入沥净血水的牛肉末煮开
  7. 加入事先调好的水淀粉勾芡，煮至汤变浓稠
  8. 夹出姜片，调小火，沿锅转圈淋入蛋白。
  9. 熄火加入盐、胡椒粉、鸡精、香菜碎和香葱碎即可。

docs.title: 小贴士
docs.text: 1 剁碎的牛肉如果直接放下锅煮就会成一坨煮不散，事先用开水在碗中烫过不 但可以把牛肉搅散，而且可以去血水。 2 勾芡的时侯不要一次倒下去，最好分两次加，先加第一次觉得不够浓稠，再 加第二次。 3 淋入蛋白的时侯，不要一碗全倒下去，而是转着圈慢慢的淋入碗内，并且火 不要开的太大了，以免把蛋白煮老了。

docs.title: Norwegian Salmon Wellington 威靈頓三文魚
docs.text:
Norwegian Salmon Wellington 威靈頓三文魚

兩件份量 Serve2 三文魚柳 2 Salmon Fillets 忌廉芝士 60g Cream Cheese 蒜頭 2cloves Garlic 洋蔥 1/4 Onion 白酒 40g White Wine 菠菜 75g Spinach 麵包糠 7g Breadcrumbs 巴馬臣芝士 15g Parmesan Cheese 酥皮 2 Puff Pastry 雞蛋 1 Egg 鹽 Salt 黑椒 Blackpepper

1.洋蔥及蒜頭去皮切碎備用 2.炒香洋蔥及蒜頭 3.洋蔥變半透明後加入白酒稍 4.轉細火加入忌廉芝士,菠菜,巴馬臣芝士及麵包糠拌勻,盛起備用 5.三文魚柳表面撒上少許鹽及黑椒 6.酥皮稍為放軟 7.三文魚放在酥皮中間，鋪上約一半份量的芝士菠菜 8.四面塗抹蛋漿,切去多餘酥皮 9.酥皮包裹三文魚,兩邊酥皮擀平後切去多餘部分再向內摺 10.反轉放在焗盤上 11.塗抹蛋漿後輕輕𠝹花 12.以200℃焗25-30分鐘即成,中途轉180°令顏色更均勻

docs.title: Thyme Butter Basted Salmon
docs.text:
Thyme Butter-Basted Salmon

Basting salmon in a mixture of butter, garlic and thyme make this salmon utterly irresistable Check out The Daily Meal's Video Network for the how-to video. 1Servings

Ingredients 1 Tablespoon olive oil 1 salmon fillet kosher salt and freshly cracked pepper 3 Tablespoons butter, cubed thyme sprigs 1 garlic cloves, crushed

Directions 1. Heat pan over medium-high heat. 2. Season salmon generously with salt and pepper. 3. Next, pour oil into pan and place salmon skin-side down; adjust heat as necessary if bottom begins to brown too quickly. Cook salmon 2-3 minutes. 4. Add butter, thyme, and garlic and let the butter melt and bubble. Begin basting the salmon, tilting the pan so that the butter juices pool together. Continue until the salmon is cooked through and opaque, about 5 minutes.

Salmon with Thyme Butter Recipe Ingredients 4 tablespoons butter, at room temperature 2 tablespoons chopped thyme 4 shallots, minced 2 pounds salmon, divided into 4 equal fillets Salt and pepper

Directions 1.Preheat oven to 400 degrees. In a small bowl, whisk together butter and thyme until well combined. 2.Tear off four pieces of aluminum foil, each double the size of a piece of salmon. 3.Place one fillet on each piece of foil. Divide butter into four parts and top each piece of salmon, first rubbing butter over the entire top of the fillet. 4.Sprinkle each fillet with chopped shallots. Season each fillet with salt and pepper. 5.Bring ends of foil up together at top of fillet and twist until sealed. Bake salmon until just cooked through, about 18-20 minutes. 6.Remove salmon from foil packet and serve warm.

Pan-Roasted Salmon with Thyme Butter Sauce This Pan-Roasted Salmon with Thyme Butter Sauce is delicious served at a small get-together or dinner party! Easy entertaining tip: Make the sauce prior to guests arriving. Ingredients 2 shallots, thinly sliced 6-7 sprigs fresh thyme Salt and pepper 2 cups white wine 1/2 cup 1 stick unsalted butter + 2 Tbsp., divided 3 Tbsp. freshly choppped thyme 4-6 6- ounce pieces salmon Sea salt and fresh ground pepper 5 Tbsp. olive oil 8 cups spinach 1 lemon Instructions To make the sauce, in a medium saucepan over medium heat, add the shallots, sprigs of thyme, and wine. Cook the sauce until reduced by three fourths. Lower the heat and add the butter, whisking until melted. Add salt and pepper and the chopped fresh thyme. Season the fish with salt and pepper. In a large saute pan over high heat, add the oil, and cook the fish for about 3 minutes on each side, until the salmon is firm (not spongy–use the back of spatula handle to press down on the salmon). At the same time, melt the 2 Tbsp. of butter in a separate saute pan. Add the spinach and cook for about 2 minutes. Squeeze fresh lemon juice on top and salt and pepper to taste. Remove the fish from pan and plate on a bed of spinach, spooning the Thyme Butter Sauce over the top of each serving. Garnish with fresh thyme and a lemon wedge. Serve!

docs.title: Capitalize All File Names In A Folder
docs.text:
powershell

# Set the target folder path
$folderPath = "C:\Your\Folder\Path"

# Get all files in the folder and rename them to uppercase
Get-ChildItem -Path $folderPath -File | ForEach-Object {
    $newName = $_.BaseName.ToUpper() + $_.Extension
    Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
}

docs.title: Comment Based Help
docs.text:
This block of text is known as Comment-Based Help (or a Help Documentation Block) in PowerShell. It allows scripts and functions to have built-in documentation that users can access directly in the console using commands like Get-Help .\MediaMaster.ps1.

<#  MediaMaster.ps1
    --------------------------------
.SYNOPSIS
    Semi-automatic controller for Merge, Split, and Encode operations.

.DESCRIPTION
    MediaMaster.ps1 orchestrates the full media pipeline:
        Merge --> Split --> Encode

.PARAMETER StartFolder
    The working directory for all operations. Default is current directory.

.PARAMETER Mode
    One or more pipeline stages: Merge, Split, Encode. Default: all three.

.PARAMETER SegmentLength
    Segment duration in seconds for splitting (default: 3000).

.PARAMETER TimestampFile
    Optional text file containing timestamps for splitting.

.PARAMETER Type
    Video filter preset for EncodeMedia ("anime", "ai-anime", "hybrid", "live"). Default: ai-anime.

.PARAMETER MaxParallel
    Maximum number of parallel encoding jobs (default: 2).

.PARAMETER DebugMode
    Enable verbose debugging output.
#>

docs.title: Manage Whitelists And Blacklists In Both Brave Shields And Ublock Origin Lite
docs.text:
1. In Brave Browser (Brave Shields)

Brave makes it very easy to whitelist or blacklist sites directly from the address bar.

How to Whitelist a Site (Allow Popups / Turn Off Blocking)

  1. Navigate to the specific website you want to allow.
  2. Click the orange Brave Shields icon (the lion head) at the right end of the address bar.
  3. Toggle the big switch at the top to "Shields are UP" so it changes to "Shields are DOWN".
  4. The page will automatically reload. Popups and ads will now be completely allowed on this specific site while remaining blocked everywhere else.

How to Blacklist a Site (Block Everything Manually)

If you want to create a custom blacklist rule to block a specific site or script:

  1. Open Brave’s settings by typing brave://settings/shields/filters into your address bar.
  2. Scroll down to the bottom to find the "Create custom filters" text box.
  3. To completely block a specific website, type: ||example.com^ (replace example.com with the site you want to block).
  4. Click Save.
  1. In Google Chrome (uBlock Origin Lite)

Because uBlock Origin Lite (the version compliant with Google's Manifest V3 rules) is streamlined, whitelisting is done through permission levels.

How to Whitelist a Site (Allow Popups / Turn Off Blocking)

  1. Navigate to the website where you need popups.
  2. Click the extension puzzle piece icon or the uBlock Origin Lite icon in your toolbar.
  3. You will see a slider showing the current filtering level for that site (Optimal, Complete, etc.).
  4. Slide it all the way down to "No Filtering" (the gray shield icon).
  5. Refresh the page. The extension is now disabled just for this specific domain.

How to Blacklist a Site (Custom Blocking)

Manifest V3 severely restricts how extensions modify lists on the fly, meaning you cannot easily type in custom text-based blocking rules inside uBlock Origin Lite like you could in the old version. If you want to block a site entirely in Chrome, it is best to use Chrome's native tools:

  1. Copy the address of the site you want to block.
  2. Go to Chrome Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings.
  3. Scroll down, click Pop-ups and redirects, and add the URL to the "Not allowed to send pop-ups or use redirects" list.

==**uBlock Origin gives you the precision to pinpoint and unblock one specific JavaScript file while keeping the rest of the site's ads blocked.

Because this requires advanced "dynamic filtering," Brave Shields is too basic for this task, Adblock Plus cannot do it due to modern extension limits, and uBlock Origin Lite cannot do it either (it lacks the advanced dynamic filtering panel). You must use a browser that supports the classic, full-featured uBlock Origin (like Firefox or Brave with Shields disabled).

uBlock Origin (Classic)

The full version of uBlock Origin includes a Live Network Logger and a Dynamic Filtering Matrix designed exactly for this scenario.

Step 1: Turn on Advanced User Mode

  1. Click the uBlock Origin icon and open the Dashboard (the gears icon).
  2. On the Settings tab, check the box next to "I am an advanced user." (Click the gears next to it if you want to see advanced settings, but just checking it is enough).

Step 2: Use the Logger to Find and Allow the Script

  1. Open the website containing the conversion function.
  2. Click the uBlock Origin icon and click the Open the logger icon (it looks like a small clipboard/list).
  3. Refresh the website page. You will see a live stream of every script loading.
  4. Look for rows highlighted in Red (these are the blocked scripts). Find the exact JavaScript file containing your conversion function.
  5. Hover your mouse over the cell in the middle column (the one showing script).
  6. Click the Gray block to set an exception rule, or click the Green block to explicitly force it to allow.
  7. Click the Padlock icon at the top left of the logger or extension popup to save this rule permanently for this site.

The Alternative: Brave Shields

Brave Shields cannot unblock a single specific JS file while keeping other ads blocked on the same page. Its engine operates on an "all or nothing" approach per script source.

Your only options inside Brave Shields are:

  • Allow all scripts: Click the Lion icon and toggle "Block Scripts" off (if you had it on), or lower Shields entirely. This lets the conversion script run, but all ads and trackers will load too.
  • Custom Filter Exception: If you know the exact URL of the script, you can try adding an exception rule in brave://settings/shields/filters using an exception modifier: @@||://example.com. However, if Brave's built-in blocklist has a broader structural rule blocking that script, local custom rules sometimes fail to override the native Rust engine.

Summary Strategy

If this conversion function is critical for your work, your best setup is to use Firefox or Brave (with Brave Shields turned off for this specific site), install the classic uBlock Origin, and use the Advanced User Network Logger to green-light that single conversion script.

docs.title: Commonly Used Characters (~3,500–6,500)
docs.text: ~70% of commonly used Traditional characters are identical in Simplified Chinese. Only about 2,235 characters were actually simplified (out of ~8,105 in the official 通用规范汉字表). So roughly 30% of high-frequency characters have a different form.

docs.title: Full Character Corpus (~50,000+)
docs.text: If you compare the entire historical corpus, the overlap is much higher — ~95–96%, since the ~2,235 simplified forms represent only a tiny fraction of all attested characters.

docs.title: Computer Character Sets
docs.text:
Set Size Notes GB2312 (Simplified) 6,763 2,311 of these are simplified forms; the rest are shared Big 5 (Traditional) 13,061 Includes many rare characters not in GB2312

The GB2312 set is largely a subset of Big 5, minus the ~2,300 characters that were replaced by simplified forms

docs.title: Bottom Line
docs.text:
For practical, everyday purposes: about 7 out of 10 common characters look exactly the same in both systems. The simplification was deliberately concentrated on high-frequency characters (which is why a Simplified-only reader can already recognize roughly half of a Traditional text on first encounter).

Chinese is not a single language but a family of mutually unintelligible varieties, officially classified into ten main dialect groups (or seven, depending on the linguistic framework). These varieties share a common written system but differ significantly in pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar.

The ten primary dialect groups are:

  1. Mandarin (65.7% of speakers): The official standard (Putonghua), spoken in northern and southwestern China.

  2. Min (6.20%): Spoken in Fujian, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia; includes Hokkien and Fuzhounese.

  3. Wu (6.10%): Spoken in Shanghai, Zhejiang, and southern Jiangsu; includes Shanghainese.

  4. Yue (5.60%): Spoken in Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macau; includes Cantonese.

  5. Jin (5.20%): Spoken in Shanxi and Inner Mongolia.

  6. Gan (3.90%): Spoken primarily in Jiangxi province.

  7. Hakka (3.50%): Spoken by scattered communities across southern China and overseas.

  8. Xiang (3.00%): Spoken in Hunan province.

  9. Huizhou (0.30%): Spoken in southern Anhui.

  10. Pinghua (0.60%): Spoken in Guangxi.

While Mandarin and Cantonese are the most widely spoken, many varieties like Wu and Min are not mutually intelligible with Mandarin or each other. Linguists estimate there are over 300 identifiable dialects, with more than 1,000 if village-level variations are included.

docs.title: Git Github Cheatsheet
docs.text: Re-push (no change in repo) Git $ git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger rebuild" Git $ git push origin [brench]

How to compare the contents of a local Git repository with the GitHub remote repository

🧩 1. Make sure your local repo knows the latest GitHub state Before comparing anything, update your remote‑tracking branches: bash $ git fetch origin This updates origin/main (or any other remote branch) without modifying your working directory.

🧩 2. Compare file‑level differences (actual content changes) A. Compare entire branches bash $ git diff main origin/main This shows line‑by‑line differences between your local main and GitHub’s origin/main. B. Compare only filenames (quick scan) bash $ git diff --name-only main origin/main C. Compare with stats bash $ git diff --stat main origin/main D. Word‑level diff bash $ git diff --color-words main origin/main

🧩 3. Compare commit history (what commits differ) A. Commits in remote but not local bash $ git log main..origin/main B. Commits in local but not remote bash $ git log origin/main..main This is useful when you want to know why the contents differ.

🧩 4. Quick summary of differences bash $ git status After git fetch, Git will tell you: “Your branch is ahead of origin/main by X commits” “Your branch is behind origin/main by X commits” “Your branch has diverged”

🧩 5. Compare specific files bash $ git diff main:path/to/file origin/main:path/to/file This isolates differences for one file or directory.

🧩 6. Visual comparison (GUI tools) If you prefer visual diffing: GitHub Desktop Sourcetree GitKraken VS Code + GitLens These tools show side‑by‑side diffs and commit graphs.

🧩 7. Practical workflow summary git fetch origin → update remote snapshot

    git diff main origin/main → compare contents

    git log main..origin/main → compare commits

    git status → quick summary

Use GUI tools if you want visual diffs

====================================================== * VS Code + GitLens

You use GitLens inside VS Code to visually compare your local Git repo with the GitHub remote repo by selecting branches/commits and running GitLens’s Compare References or Inspect features. This gives you a clean, side‑by‑side diff viewer with file‑level and line‑level changes.

Below is the full workflow, grounded in the sources you saw.

🔧 Install GitLens (if not already installed) Open VS Code

Go to Extensions

Search GitLens

Click Install (GitLens is maintained by GitKraken and enhances Git inside VS Code.)

🧩 Compare Local vs GitHub Using GitLens 1. Make sure your local repo knows the GitHub remote Before comparing anything, update your remote‑tracking branches:

bash git fetch origin This ensures origin/main (GitHub) is up to date.

🟦 Method A — Compare Branches (Local vs Remote) GitLens provides a built‑in Compare References feature.

Steps Open VS Code

Click the GitLens icon in the Activity Bar

Go to Search & Compare

Select Compare References

Choose:

Local branch → e.g., main

Remote branch → e.g., origin/main (GitHub)

GitLens will generate a full diff report showing:

Added lines (green)

Removed lines (red)

Modified lines (blue)

This is the cleanest way to compare your local Git repo with GitHub.

🟦 Method B — Compare Commits (Local commit vs GitHub commit) GitLens lets you compare any two commits visually.

Steps Open GitLens → Inspect tab

Enter the base commit SHA (local or remote)

Click Select for Compare

Enter the second commit SHA

Click Open All Changes

GitLens shows a file‑by‑file diff viewer.

🟦 Method C — Use the Commit Graph (visual history) GitLens’s Commit Graph shows:

Local commits

Remote commits

Ahead/behind status

Unpushed/unpulled changes

You can right‑click any commit and choose Compare with…

🟦 Method D — Compare Individual Files Right‑click any file → GitLens: Open Changes You can compare:

Working tree vs HEAD

Local branch vs remote branch

Specific commit vs another commit

🧠 What this gives you (practical benefits) Visual diff instead of terminal diff

Clear color‑coded changes

Easy navigation between changed files

Ability to compare local vs GitHub without manually running git diff

Faster debugging and version control review

🏁 Summary To compare repository contents between Git (local) and GitHub (remote) using VS Code + GitLens:

git fetch origin

GitLens → Search & Compare → Compare References

Select main vs origin/main

Review the visual diff viewer

This is the most accurate and user‑friendly way to compare repo contents.

docs.title: Step‑by‑Step Upgrade on PythonAnywhere
docs.text:
📝 Migration Checklist: Flask Project Upgrade 🔍 Pre‑Upgrade Prep - [ ] Clone your project (Git or manual copy) so you have a safe rollback. - [ ] Freeze dependencies: pip freeze > requirements.txt - [ ] Check library compatibility: Verify that Flask, SQLAlchemy, Jinja2, and any niche packages support Python 3.12/3.13. - [ ] Upgrade local environment first: Install Python 3.12/3.13 locally and run your app/tests there before touching PythonAnywhere.

⚙️ Environment Setup - [ ] Create new virtualenv on PythonAnywhere: mkvirtualenv --python=/usr/bin/python3.12 flask312 - (or /usr/bin/python3.13 for 3.13). - [ ] Reinstall dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt - [ ] Update Web tab config: Point your Flask app to the new virtualenv path. - [ ] Reload app in PythonAnywhere. 🧪 Testing & Validation- [ ] Run pytest locally and on PythonAnywhere to confirm all tests pass. - [ ] Check logs (error log, server log) for warnings or incompatibilities. - [ ] Verify WSGI file still points to the correct Flask app entry point. - [ ] Test routes manually (login, forms, API endpoints) to confirm runtime behavior. 🛠️ Coding Considerations- Deprecations: Python 3.12/3.13 remove or warn about older APIs. Watch for: - distutils (deprecated — use setuptools). - Old asyncio patterns (some APIs changed). - collections aliases (e.g., collections.Mapping → collections.abc.Mapping). - Type hints: Python 3.12/3.13 improve typing; if you use type checking, update annotations. - Error messages: Tracebacks are more detailed — helpful, but may expose more info in logs. - Third‑party packages: Some C‑extension packages may need recompilation under the new interpreter. 🔒 Config & Deployment Notes- [ ] Check system image: Ensure you’re on PythonAnywhere’s latest image (Ubuntu 22.04) to access 3.12/3.13. - [ ] Database drivers: If you use MySQL/Postgres, confirm driver compatibility with the new Python version. - [ ] Gunicorn/WSGI: Reinstall in the new virtualenv (pip install gunicorn). - [ ] Static files: Verify Flask’s static file serving works as expected after upgrade. - [ ] Backup old env: Keep your 3.10 virtualenv until you’re confident everything works. 🚀 Rollback Plan- If something breaks, simply switch your PythonAnywhere Web tab back to the old 3.10 virtualenv. - No code changes needed — just reload the app.

================================================================================= 1. Check Your Current System Image - Log into PythonAnywhere. - Go to Account → System Image. - If you’re on an older image (Ubuntu 20.04), you’ll only see Python up to 3.10. - To access 3.12 or 3.13, you need the latest image (Ubuntu 22.04 base). - If available, click Upgrade system image. - Note: upgrading may require reinstalling packages, so plan carefully.

  1. Create a New Virtual Environment Once the newer Python version is available: mkvirtualenv --python=/usr/bin/python3.12 myflaskenv

  2. Replace myflaskenv with your project’s environment name.

  3. This creates a clean environment tied to Python 3.12.

  4. If you want 3.13 instead, change the path to /usr/bin/python3.13.

  5. Reinstall Dependencies

  6. In your new virtualenv, reinstall everything from your project’s requirements: pip install -r requirements.txt

  7. If you don’t have a requirements.txt, generate one locally first: pip freeze > requirements.txt

This ensures your PythonAnywhere environment matches your local setup.

  1. Update Your Web App Configuration
  2. Go to the Web tab in PythonAnywhere.
  3. Under Virtualenv, point your app to the new environment (/home/yourusername/.virtualenvs/myflaskenv).

  4. Reload the web app.

  5. Test Thoroughly

  6. Run your app locally under Python 3.12 (or 3.13) first.
  7. Use pytest or your test suite to confirm everything works.

  8. Deploy to PythonAnywhere and check logs (error log and server log) for issues.

  9. Clean Up

  10. Once you’re confident the new environment works, you can delete the old 3.10 virtualenv to save space.
  11. Keep your requirements.txt updated so future upgrades are easier.

🚨 Things to Watch - Library compatibility → Most Flask ecosystem libraries support 3.12/3.13, but double‑check if you use niche packages. - Local vs Remote match → Upgrade your local environment to the same Python version (3.12.x or 3.13.x) so you don’t hit “works locally but not remotely” issues. - System image upgrade → This is the critical step. Without upgrading your PythonAnywhere system image, you won’t see newer Python interpreters.

👉 In short: - Upgrade your PythonAnywhere system image. - Create a new virtualenv with Python 3.12 (or 3.13). - Reinstall dependencies. - Point your Flask app to the new env. - Test and clean up.

================================================================================= 🛠️ Safe Upgrade Workflow with Visual Studio + PythonAnywhere 1. Clone Your Project - In Visual Studio (or Git), make a fresh clone of your repo: git clone flask-upgrade - This gives you a separate working copy (flask-upgrade) where you can test Python 3.12/3.13.

  1. Create a New Virtual Environment
  2. Locally: python3.12 -m venv venv312
  3. or python3.13 -m venv venv313
  4. Activate it and reinstall dependencies: source venv312/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt
  5. Test Locally First- Run your Flask app under the new Python version: flask run
  6. Use pytest to confirm your test suite passes.

  7. Fix any dependency issues before touching PythonAnywhere.

  9. Upgrade on PythonAnywhere- Create a new virtualenv tied to Python 3.12 or 3.13: mkvirtualenv --python=/usr/bin/python3.12 flask312
  10. Reinstall dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt
  11. In the Web tab, point your app to the new virtualenv.
  12. Reload the app.
  13. Keep the Old Environment as Backup- Don’t delete your Python 3.10 virtualenv right away.
  14. If something breaks, you can quickly switch back in the Web tab. 🚀 Why This Works- Cloning → You isolate the upgrade experiment from your stable project.
  15. Virtualenvs → You can switch between Python versions easily.
  16. Testing locally first → You catch issues before deploying.
  17. Rollback safety → Your 3.10 environment remains intact until you’re confident. 👉 In short: Yes, clone the project, upgrade in the clone, test locally, then deploy to PythonAnywhere. That way you’re always one step ahead without risking downtime.Would you like me to draft a migration checklist (like a Git + PythonAnywhere playbook) so you can tick off each step as you move from 3.10 → 3.12/3.13?

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
VerifyMedia.ps1 validates one pair of media files:

Code

original.mp4
encoded.mp4

It performs structural QC checks using ffprobe:

  • Video duration

  • Frame count

  • FPS

  • Audio duration

Then determines whether the encoded file matches the original.

This script is designed to be:

  • Fast (≈5 seconds for a 2‑hour video)

  • Modular

  • Script‑friendly

  • Human‑readable (Detail mode)

  • Machine‑readable (JSON mode)

It is the core building block used by VerifyBatch.ps1.

docs.title: 1. Input
docs.text:
You provide:

Code

-Original "video.mp4"
-Encoded "video_encoded.mp4"

docs.title: 2. ffprobe Metrics Collected
docs.text:
The script extracts:

Metric Description Duration Total video length in seconds Frame Count Total number of decoded frames FPS Frames per second (r_frame_rate) Audio Duration Length of audio stream

docs.title: 3. Matching Logic
docs.text:
Each metric is compared:

  • Duration → must match within ±0.01 seconds

  • Frame count → must match exactly

  • FPS → must match within ±0.01

  • Audio duration → must match within ±0.01 seconds

If all four match:

Code

AllMatch = True

Otherwise:

Code

AllMatch = False

docs.title: Default (Boolean)
docs.text:
Returns only:

Code

True

or

Code

False

Perfect for scripting and automation.

docs.title: Mode Detail
docs.text:
Prints human‑readable metrics:

  • Original vs encoded values

  • Match flags

  • Overall match

  • Timestamp

  • File names

Useful for debugging individual files.

docs.title: Mode Json
docs.text:
Returns a JSON object containing:

  • Original filename

  • Encoded filename

  • Verification timestamp

  • All numeric metrics

  • Match flags

  • Overall match

Ideal for logging, dashboards, batch QC, and machine parsing.

docs.title: ✔ 1. Boolean mode (default)
docs.text:
Fast QC for automation:

powershell

$verified = .\VerifyMedia.ps1 -Original "video.mp4" -Encoded "video_encoded.mp4"

if ($verified) {
    Write-Host "Verification passed."
} else {
    Write-Host "Verification FAILED."
}

Output:

Code

True

or

Code

False

docs.title: ⏱ Performance: How long does verification take?
For a 2‑hour video:
docs.text:
Operation Time Duration < 0.01 sec FPS < 0.01 sec Audio duration < 0.01 sec Frame count 3–15 seconds

Frame count is the only expensive step because ffprobe must decode every frame.

docs.title: Real‑world total time:
docs.text:
≈ 5 seconds per 2‑hour video (on your workstation)

This is extremely efficient for structural QC.

docs.title: VerifyBatch.ps1 builds on this to handle entire folders.
🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
VerifyBatch.ps1 automates verification of multiple encoded videos inside a folder. It detects file pairs using the naming pattern:

Code

media.mp4
media_encoded.mp4

Then it calls VerifyMedia.ps1 for each pair and returns:

  • Boolean match (default)

  • Detailed metrics (Mode Detail)

  • JSON logs (Mode Json)

This is your batch QC layer.

docs.title: 1. Input
docs.text:
You provide:

Code

-StartFolder "C:\Workspace\Done"

docs.title: 2. File Pair Detection
docs.text:
It scans the folder for:

Code

*_encoded.mp4

For each encoded file:

Code

video1_encoded.mp4 → video1.mp4
video2_encoded.mp4 → video2.mp4

If the original file is missing, it skips the pair.

docs.title: 3. Verification
docs.text:
For each pair:

Code

VerifyMedia.ps1 -Original video1.mp4 -Encoded video1_encoded.mp4

docs.title: 4. Output
docs.text: Depending on mode:

docs.title: Default (Boolean)
docs.text:
Returns a summary table:

Code

Original                Encoded                     Match
--------                -------                     -----
video1.mp4             video1_encoded.mp4           True
video2.mp4             video2_encoded.mp4           False

docs.title: Mode Detail
docs.text: Prints full metrics for each pair.

docs.title: Mode Json
docs.text:
Creates JSON logs:

Code

Verify_video1.json
Verify_video2.json

And returns a summary table.

Each pair prints:

Useful for debugging individual files.

Each JSON includes:

  • Duration

Perfect for:

docs.title: 🧱 Integration Example (EncodeMedia.ps1)
docs.text:
After encoding all files:

$batchResult = .\VerifyBatch.ps1 -StartFolder $StartFolder -Mode Json

# Optional: check if all passed

    Write-Host "Some files failed verification."
} else {
    Write-Host "All files verified successfully."
}

docs.text:
This is the complete list that’s outputted by ffmpeg when running ffmpeg -h full. (Originall From: Posted 2015-05-29 http://ubwg.net/b/full-list-of-ffmpeg-flags-and-options) usage: ffmpeg [options] [[infile options] -i infile]… {[outfile options] outfile}…

Getting help: -h — print basic options -h long — print more options -h full — print all options (including all format and codec specific options, very long) See man ffmpeg for detailed description of the options.

Print help / information / capabilities: -L show license -h topic show help -? topic show help -help topic show help —help topic show help -version show version -buildconf show build configuration -formats show available formats -codecs show available codecs -decoders show available decoders -encoders show available encoders -bsfs show available bit stream filters -protocols show available protocols -filters show available filters -pix_fmts show available pixel formats -layouts show standard channel layouts -sample_fmts show available audio sample formats -colors show available color names

Global options (affect whole program instead of just one file): -loglevel loglevel set logging level -v loglevel set logging level -report generate a report -max_alloc bytes set maximum size of a single allocated block -y overwrite output files -n never overwrite output files -stats print progress report during encoding -max_error_rate ratio of errors (0.0: no errors, 1.0: 100% error maximum error rate -bits_per_raw_sample number set the number of bits per raw sample -vol volume change audio volume (256=normal)

Advanced global options: -cpuflags flags force specific cpu flags -hide_banner hide_banner do not show program banner -benchmark add timings for benchmarking -benchmark_all add timings for each task -progress url write program-readable progress information -stdin enable or disable interaction on standard input -timelimit limit set max runtime in seconds -dump dump each input packet -hex when dumping packets, also dump the payload -vsync video sync method -async audio sync method -adrift_threshold threshold audio drift threshold -copyts copy timestamps -copytb mode copy input stream time base when stream copying -dts_delta_threshold threshold timestamp discontinuity delta threshold -dts_error_threshold threshold timestamp error delta threshold -xerror error exit on error -filter_complex graph_description create a complex filtergraph -lavfi graph_description create a complex filtergraph -filter_complex_script filename read complex filtergraph description from a file -debug_ts print timestamp debugging info -intra deprecated use -g 1 -vdt n discard threshold -sameq Removed -same_quant Removed -deinterlace this option is deprecated, use the yadif filter instead -psnr calculate PSNR of compressed frames -vstats dump video coding statistics to file -vstats_file file dump video coding statistics to file -dc precision intra_dc_precision -qphist show QP histogram -vc channel deprecated, use -channel -tvstd standard deprecated, use -standard -isync this option is deprecated and does nothing -override_ffserver override the options from ffserver

Per-file main options: -f fmt force format -c codec codec name -codec codec codec name -pre preset preset name -map_metadata outfile[,metadata]:infile[,metadata] set metadata information of outfile from infile -t duration record or transcode “duration” seconds of audio/video -to time_stop record or transcode stop time -fs limit_size set the limit file size in bytes -ss time_off set the start time offset -timestamp time set the recording timestamp (‘now’ to set the current time) -metadata string=string add metadata -target type specify target file type (“vcd”, “svcd”, “dvd”, “dv”, “dv50”, “pal-vcd”, “ntsc-svcd”, …) -apad audio pad -frames number set the number of frames to record -filter filter_graph set stream filtergraph -filter_script filename read stream filtergraph description from a file -reinit_filter reinit filtergraph on input parameter changes

Video options: -vframes number set the number of video frames to record -r rate set frame rate (Hz value, fraction or abbreviation) -s size set frame size (WxH or abbreviation) -aspect aspect set aspect ratio (4:3, 16:9 or 1.3333, 1.7777) -bits_per_raw_sample number set the number of bits per raw sample -vn disable video -vcodec codec force video codec (‘copy’ to copy stream) -timecode hh:mm:ss[:;.]ff set initial TimeCode value. -pass n select the pass number (1 to 3) -vf filter_graph set video filters -b bitrate video bitrate (please use -b:v) -dn disable data

docs.title: Filter Chain
docs.text:
def get_video_filter(video_type: str, log_file: Path, debug_mode: bool) -> str:

    # Returns the appropriate video filter chain based on the video type preset.

        # resize video to 854 x 480

        preset = "format=yuv420p,
        scale='if(gte(iw,ih),min(iw,960),-2)':'if(gte(iw,ih),-2,min(ih,960))',"

        v_type = video_type.lower()



        if v_type == "anime":

            filters = preset + "unsharp=3:3:0.5,hqdn3d=1.0:1.0:4:4"

        elif v_type == "ai-anime":

            filters = preset + "unsharp=3:3:0.4,hqdn3d=1.2:1.2:5:5"

        elif v_type == "hybrid":

            filters = preset + "unsharp=3:3:0.35,hqdn3d=0.9:0.9:4:4"

        elif v_type == "live":

            filters = preset + "unsharp=3:3:0.3,hqdn3d=0.7:0.7:3:3"

        else:

            write_log(log_file, "WARNING", f"Unknown type '{video_type}'. Using 'ai-anime' preset.", debug_mode)

            filters = preset + "unsharp=3:3:0.4,hqdn3d=1.2:1.2:5:5"



        return filters

 filter_chain = get_video_filter(video_type, log_file, debug_mode)
 ffmpeg_cmd = [
        "ffmpeg",
        "-hide_banner",
        "-loglevel", loglevel,
        "-report",
        "-i", str(file_path),
        "-vf", filter_chain,
        "-c:v", "libx265",
        "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le",
        "-crf", "26",
        "-preset", "medium",
        "-c:a", "aac",
        "-b:a", "64k",
        str(out_path)
        }

docs.title: Media Processing Workflow Toolset
docs.text: This document details the complete Python-based media processing pipeline refactored for high performance, Windows priority management, non-ASCII metadata resilience, and automated verification.

docs.title: 1. media_utils.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Serves as the core utility module shared across all scripts. It standardizes log formatting, guarantees UTF-8 safe execution of subprocesses (preventing non-ASCII encoding crashes), and manages Windows process priority.
  • Usage: Imported as a library module by other Python scripts (from media_utils import write_log, run_ffmpeg).
  • Constraints:
  • Must reside in the same directory as the executing scripts.
  • Operating System: Windows (ctypes.windll.kernel32 used for BelowNormal process priority; falls back to os.nice on UNIX).
  • Requires ffmpeg and ffprobe to be accessible in the system's PATH.

docs.title: 2. MergeMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Scans a directory for matching media components (video, audio, subtitles) grouped by base filename and stream-copies them into unified .mkv container files.
  • Usage: 
    python MergeMedia.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" [--DebugMode]
  • Constraints:
  • Automatically ignores files starting with merged_, MergeMedia_, or SplitMedia_.
  • Preserves original stream codecs using -c copy.
  • Subtitle files (.srt, .ass, .vtt) should be encoded in UTF-8 to prevent container-level character mapping issues.
  • Output files follow the naming convention merged_<basename>.mkv.

docs.title: 3. SplitMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Batch splits media files into smaller segments using either fixed-length durations or exact timestamp sequences.
  • Usage:
  • Fixed-length mode: 
    python SplitMedia.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" --SegmentLength 3000
  • Timestamp-based mode: 
    python SplitMedia.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" --TimestampFile "timestamps.txt"
  • Constraints:
  • Automatically target-matches files prefixed with merged_ when --Original is not explicitly declared.
  • Stream-copies video without re-encoding (-c copy).
  • Output segment pattern follows split_<basename>_p00.mkv.
  • Timestamp files must contain at least two valid timestamp lines (HH:MM:SS or seconds).

docs.title: 4. EncodeMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Encodes video segments using libx265 (10-bit color depth) and configurable video filtering presets (ai-anime, anime, hybrid, live) with parallel processing support.
  • Usage: 
    python EncodeMedia.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" --Type ai-anime --MaxParallel 2 --OutputFormat mkv [--enableFrameCheck] [--DebugMode]
  • Constraints:
  • Automatically scans for target input files starting with split_.
  • Outputs files with the prefix encoded_<basename>.<format>.
  • Requires sufficient CPU/GPU capacity depending on the --MaxParallel threshold.
  • Automatically triggers VerifyMedia.py post-encoding for quality assurance.

docs.title: 5. VerifyMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Performs structural quality control checks on a pair of media files (original vs. encoded) by inspecting stream metadata via ffprobe. Validates video duration, frame rate (FPS), audio duration, and frame counts.
  • Usage: 
    python VerifyMedia.py --Original "split_file_p00.mkv" --Encoded "encoded_file_p00.mkv" [--enableFrameCheck] [--Mode Detail|Json]
  • Constraints:
  • Frame count verification (--enableFrameCheck) requires reading all video frames with ffprobe (-count_frames) and is disabled by default for optimal performance.
  • Falls back to global container format duration if individual stream duration headers are missing or evaluate to 0.

docs.title: 6. VerifyMediaBatch.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Discovers all encoded_* files within a directory, pairs them with their corresponding split_* source files, runs validation checks, and compiles summary reports or aggregated JSON logs.
  • Usage: 
    python VerifyMediaBatch.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" [--enableFrameCheck] [--Mode Json]
  • Constraints:
  • Expects file naming alignment (encoded_<name> matching back to split_<name>).
  • Generates VerifyMediaBatch.json in the target directory when run in Json mode.

docs.title: 7. MediaMaster.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Pipeline controller that orchestrates the entire workflow (Merge $\rightarrow$ Split $\rightarrow$ Encode) in strict sequence while validating component presence before each stage.
  • Usage: 
    python MediaMaster.py --StartFolder "D:\MediaFolder" --Mode Merge Split Encode --Type ai-anime --MaxParallel 2
  • Constraints:
  • Enforces fixed execution ordering regardless of input parameter sequence.
  • Skips stages dynamically if required prerequisites (video.*/audio.*, merged_*, split_*) are absent from --StartFolder.
  • Calls sub-scripts as standalone Python subprocesses within the working runtime environment.

docs.title: Overview of Generated Metadata:
docs.text:
• media_utils.py: Details UTF-8 stream decoding, process priority management (0x00004000 for BelowNormal), and shared logger mechanics.

  • MergeMedia.py / SplitMedia.py / EncodeMedia.py: Covers dynamic parameters, file discovery rules, input/output prefixes (merged_, split_, encoded_), and encoding specifications.

  • VerifyMedia.py / VerifyMediaBatch.py: Summarizes performance considerations (bypassing -count_frames by default), fallback audio metadata checks, and JSON output structures.

  • MediaMaster.py: Explains stage validation and pipeline automation logic.

If you just want to change containers (e.g., .mkv to .mp4) instantly **without quality loss or re-encoding. For a quick, lossless container switch, a simple one-line FFmpeg copy command is much faster: ffmpeg -i input.mkv -c copy output.mp4

docs.title: Development Specification (Dev Spec)
docs.text: Below is the complete Technical & Architectural Specification for your Windows-based Python media processing pipeline.

docs.title: 1. System Architecture & Philosophy
docs.text:
• Language / Environment: Python 3.x, designed for native execution on Windows 11.

  • Core Design Patterns:

    • Modular Decoupling: Shared utilities and process management reside in media_utils.py. Individual steps operate as standalone scripts or orchestrated children under MediaMaster.py.

    • Late Container Binding: Universal processing and heavy manipulation (merging/splitting) take place inside the flexible .mkv container, deferring final container selection (.mkv or .mp4) to the encoding stage.

    • Resource Politeness: Background FFmpeg tasks run at BelowNormal process priority (0x00004000) via Windows ctypes API calls to prevent system thread thrashing.

docs.title: 2. File Naming & Prefix Conventions
docs.text:
The pipeline relies on predictable naming standards to track assets across stages:

  • Raw Inputs: video.*, audio.*, *.srt/.ass/.vtt

  • Merged State: merged_<basename>.mkv

  • Split Segments: split_<basename>_p00.mkv, split_<basename>_p01.mkv, etc.

  • Encoded Output: encoded_<basename>_p00.mkv (or .mp4)

  • Verification Reports: VerifyMediaBatch.json

docs.title: media_utils.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Centralized logging (write_log) and safe process spawning (run_ffmpeg).

  • Key Mechanisms:

    • Enforces UTF-8 stream decoding with errors="replace" to handle non-ASCII characters smoothly.

    • Adjusts process priority to BelowNormal (0x00004000) using ctypes.windll.kernel32.SetPriorityClass on Windows platforms.

docs.title: MergeMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Automatically groups corresponding video, audio, and subtitle streams by base name and muxes them into .mkv format using stream copy (-c copy).

  • Constraints: Requires at least a video stream paired with an audio or subtitle stream to execute.

docs.title: SplitMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Divides merged files either by a fixed segment length (default: 3000 seconds) or via an external timestamp text file.

  • Constraints: Relies on stream copying (-c copy) for rapid, lossless segmentation.

docs.title: EncodeMedia.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Transcodes split files using libx265 (10-bit color yuv420p10le, CRF 26) with dynamic video filter chains (ai-anime, anime, hybrid, live).

  • Concurrency: Executes jobs in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor governed by --MaxParallel.

  • Quality Control Integration: Automatically invokes VerifyMedia.py upon completing each file encode.

docs.title: VerifyMedia.py & VerifyMediaBatch.py
docs.text:
• Purpose: Post-encoding structural quality control via ffprobe.

  • Performance Optimization: Heavy frame-counting checks (-count_frames) are strictly disabled by default, and only run when --enableFrameCheck is explicitly provided.

docs.title: Why Obsidian works so well with AI
docs.text: Obsidian is basically a single local folder, called a vault, full of markdown (.md) files. Open the folder in Obsidian and you get a clean interface for reading and writing notes, but under the hood it's still just plain text files sitting on your computer.

docs.title: Level 1: The AI Second Brain
docs.text: This is the classic second brain concept (popularized by Tiago Forte), just upgraded. You still write the notes yourself. The difference is that instead of manually searching your own vault, an AI retrieves, analyzes, and interprets the information for you.

docs.title: How to build it
docs.text:
• Step 1: Create a folder and turn it into an Obsidian vault.
  • Step 2: Add three .md files so the AI can navigate: ME.md (who you are, what you optimize for, how to talk to you), MAP.md (how your folders and notes are structured), and SKILLS.md (what you want the AI to be able to do).
  • Step 3: Put your actual notes in a notes/ subfolder as .md files.
  • Step 4: Put raw data (screenshots, stats, exports) in an evidence/ subfolder.
  • Step 5: Connect an AI. General local agents like Claude Cowork, OpenClaw, or Hermes work well for conversational use. Coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode are better if you want to build something programmatically (dashboards, apps) from your notes. For full privacy, use an open-source agent harness with a local model.

docs.title: Level 2: The AI Database
docs.text: This flips level 1 around: AI writes the notes into your vault, and you (or another AI) read them. This is the setup for people like me who don't want to write notes themselves but still want a rich, searchable record. Multiple AI agents across multiple machines can all write to the same vault at once, since Obsidian Sync keeps everything updated and encrypted. My go-to models for this kind of writing are Gemini Flash and DeepSeek V3, or Qwen 3 32B running locally for full privacy.

docs.title: How to build it
docs.text:
• Step 1: Create a folder and Obsidian vault.
  • Step 2: Point one or more AI agents at it with write access.
  • Step 3: Let the AI file what it writes into .md files: research, meeting notes, saved articles, daily logs.
  • Step 4: Browse, search, and link things by hand using Obsidian's search, graph view, and backlinks.
  • Step 5 (optional): Connect another AI agent to retrieve, analyze, and interpret the data for you, the same way you would in a second brain.

docs.title: Level 3: The LLM Wiki
docs.text: This is the full setup, a concept coined by Andrej Karpathy. You don't touch the vault at all. AI writes the notes, manages the whole thing, and retrieves and interprets it for you. As Karpathy puts it: Obsidian is the IDE, the AI is the programmer, and the vault is the codebase. You're just the observer.

docs.title: The three layers
docs.text:
Raw sources

Your curated, immutable collection of articles, papers, images, and data. The AI reads these but never modifies them. This is your source of truth.

Wiki

AI-generated markdown files: summaries, entity pages, comparisons, overviews. The AI owns this layer completely and updates it as new sources arrive.

Schema

A file like claude.md or agents.md that tells the AI how the wiki is structured and how to navigate the corpus.

docs.title: The three operations
docs.text:
• Ingest: drop a new source into raw sources and tell the AI to process it.
  • Query: ask questions against the wiki; the AI searches, reads, and synthesizes an answer.
  • Lint: the AI health-checks the wiki, resolving contradictions, flagging stale claims, and cleaning up orphaned pages.

Two special files help both you and the AI navigate as the wiki grows: index.md (a content-oriented catalog of every page, with summaries and metadata) and log.md (a chronological, append-only record of every ingest, query, and lint the AI has run).

docs.title: Who this is for
docs.text: Karpathy describes several use cases: personal tracking (goals, health, self-improvement), deep research on a topic over weeks or months, reading a book and building out character or theme pages as you go, internal team wikis fed by Slack and meeting transcripts, and things like competitive analysis, trip planning, or hobby deep dives, basically anything where knowledge accumulates over time and you want it organized instead of scattered.

docs.title: How to build it
docs.text:
• Step 1: Create a folder and Obsidian vault.
  • Step 2: Pick an AI and implement its LLM wiki skill. I used Hermes, which has this built in as a skill. Claude Code is the most documented option, with GitHub repos you can clone and run directly. Codex and OpenCode also work.
  • Step 3: Try ingesting a few sources and let the AI take care of filing them.
  • Step 4: Let it run autonomously over time, ingesting, querying, and linting on its own.

docs.title: Configurate Anythingllm
docs.text:
To connect your local Ollama engine running Gemma 4 12B to AnythingLLM, you will configure two main sections within the settings menu: the LLM Provider (the model that talks to you) and the Embedding Provider (the model that processes your files).

Here is the exact step-by-step configuration layout to match your memory-safe 16GB RAM laptop setup:

Step 1: LLM Configuration (The Chat Engine)

Navigate to Settings (the gear icon on the bottom left) > LLM Provider, select Ollama, and input the following details:

  • Ollama Base URL: http://localhost:11434
  • Model: Select gemma4:12b from the dropdown list. (If it doesn't appear, ensure your batch script is running and click the refresh icon).
  • Token Context Window: 8192 (Though Gemma 4 supports much higher windows, limiting this to 8K or 16K ensures your 16GB CPU-only system doesn't run out of memory during very long conversations).

Step 2: Embedding Configuration (The Document Parser)

Navigate to Settings > Embedding Provider. Since you are on a 16GB CPU-only machine, using a heavy local model for embedding can lag your system. Do not use Gemma 4 for embeddings. Use a specialized, lightweight embedding model instead.

Select Ollama and input these details:

  • Ollama Base URL: http://localhost:11434
  • Embedding Model: nomic-embed-text (Open your Windows terminal and run ollama pull nomic-embed-text if you don't have it. It takes up less than 300MB of RAM and runs lighting-fast on your CPU).
  • Max Embedding Chunk Length: 512

Step 3: Vector Database (The Librarian Memory)

Navigate to Settings > Vector Database.

  • Vector Database Provider: Select System Architecture (Default).
  • This locks in the built-in, disk-saving LanceDB instance we discussed, ensuring zero extra RAM overhead.

Step 4: Workspace Adjustments (Fine-Tuning)

Once your system-wide settings are saved, go back to your main dashboard and click New Workspace (e.g., name it "AI-Librarian"). Click the Workspace Settings gear next to its name to apply these crucial tweaks:

  • Chat Temperature: 0.2 (For the Librarian setup, keeping this low prevents the model from hallucinating or making up facts not found in your notes/manuals).
  • LLM Thinking Mode: Disabled (Toggle Off). (Turning off the deep chain-of-thought "thinking" mode gives your i7 CPU pure text speed. If you have a highly complex logic problem, you can toggle it back on temporarily).

To link your local Obsidian Vault folder directly into your AnythingLLM workspace, you will use AnythingLLM's local folder connector. This allows the application to read your markdown .md files straight from your computer's hard drive.

Here is the exact step-by-step process to link them:

Step 1: Open the Document Manager

  1. Open AnythingLLM and click on your AI-Librarian workspace in the left sidebar.
  2. Click on the Upload / Manage Documents icon (it looks like a folder with an arrow or a cloud icon) located right below the workspace name or near the top of the chat area.

Step 2: Use the Local Folder Importer

  1. Inside the document manager window, look at the left-hand column under the upload zones.
  2. Click on Import Local Folder or click the Folder icon option.
  3. A file browser window will pop up. Navigate to where your local Obsidian Vault is saved on your hard drive (e.g., C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME\Documents\MyObsidianVault).
  4. Select the root folder of your vault and click Select Folder / Open.

Step 3: Pin or Move Your Notes to the Workspace

  1. Once imported, you will see your entire Obsidian folder structure appear in the left-hand file tree of the AnythingLLM document manager.
  2. Check the box next to your main Obsidian folder (or check individual sub-folders like "Notes" or "Manuals").
  3. Click the Move to Workspace button in the middle of the screen. This stages your markdown files, preparing them to be read by your local database.

Step 4: Run the Embed Pipeline

  1. Click the green Save and Embed button at the bottom right of the window.
  2. What happens now: AnythingLLM will read your Obsidian markdown files, use your nomic-embed-text model via Ollama to turn the text into vector math, and store those math coordinates cleanly inside the built-in LanceDB.

Crucial Tip for 16GB Memory & CPU Stability

Because you are using an 11th Gen Intel CPU without a dedicated GPU, processing hundreds of notes all at once can max out your machine temporarily.

To prevent your laptop from choking during the initial embedding process:

  • Turn on your run-ollama.bat script first: This ensures that the embedding process runs at BelowNormal priority. If you need to check an email or use your browser while AnythingLLM is indexing your vault, your laptop will stay completely smooth and responsive.
  • Do a bulk upload once, then sync: If you add new notes to Obsidian later, simply open this document manager window again and click the Resync / Sync button next to your folder. AnythingLLM will smartly scan for only the new or modified files rather than re-processing your entire vault from scratch.

For 16GB RAM

docs.title: Key Variables to Set in System Variables:
docs.text:
• OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS = 2 (Allows 1 LLM + 1 Embedding model simultaneously without thrashing memory)

  • OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL = 1 (Prevents memory usage from doubling per process)

  • OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE = q8_0 (Cuts memory usage for context windows roughly in half)

How to set System Variables in Windows:

Press Win + R $\$rightarrow type sysdm.cpl $\$rightarrow open Advanced tab $\rightarrow$ click Environment Variables $\rightarrow$ add/edit under the System variables panel (bottom section).

docs.title: 2. Fine-Tuning AnythingLLM Memory Settings (For 16GB RAM)
docs.text: In AnythingLLM, "memory" refers to both Vector Database Retrieval (RAG) and Chat History retention. On a 16GB System running local LLMs, fine-tuning these settings stops the application from overwhelming your available system RAM or overflowing your model's context window.

docs.title: A. Chat History Depth (Conversation Memory)
docs.text:
• Location: Workspace Settings $\rightarrow$ Chat Settings $\rightarrow$ Chat History

  • Recommended Setting: 4 to 6 turns

  • Why: AnythingLLM re-sends previous messages back to Ollama on every new request to give the model memory. If set to 15–20 turns, long troubleshooting threads will send thousands of extra tokens per prompt, causing high memory usage and latency. Setting it between 4 and 6 retains essential conversation flow without wasting memory.

docs.title: B. Document Chunk Size & Overlap (Text Splitter)
docs.text:
• Location: Settings (Gear icon) $\rightarrow$ AI Providers $\rightarrow$ Text Splitter & Chunking

  • Recommended Settings:

    • Text Chunk Size: 1000 characters (~250 tokens)

    • Text Chunk Overlap: 50 to 100 characters

  • Why: nomic-embed-text handles chunks around 1,000 characters cleanly. Overly large chunks force higher RAM usage during vector search, while overly small chunks fragment document context.

docs.title: C. Vector Database Retrieval Density (RAG Snippets)
docs.text:
• Location: Workspace Settings $\rightarrow$ Vector Database Settings $\rightarrow$ Max Context Snippets

  • Recommended Setting: 4 to 5 snippets

  • Why: Controls how many relevant document paragraphs AnythingLLM injects into your prompt when searching attached files. 4 to 5 snippets provide strong document grounding without overwhelming your model context.

docs.title: 3. Reviewing Your Startup Batch Script
docs.text: Your updated batch script is clean and properly formatted! Commenting out nomic-embed-text from the keep_alive: 0 flush step ensures it stays warm in RAM alongside your active chat model when setting OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2.

docs.title: Minor Fix for the nomic-embed-text Comment Line
docs.text: In Windows .bat / .cmd scripts, lines beginning with # can throw a syntax error or output warnings because # is not a standard Windows batch comment operator (batch uses :: or rem).

docs.title: Free Open Source Ai Models
docs.text:
A.K.A Open-Weight models

⚡ Lightweight & Edge Models (Best for Laptops & Single GPUs)

These models are highly efficient, require minimal RAM, and are perfectly optimized to run smoothly on standard laptops or everyday consumer devices. [1, 2, 3]

  • Google Gemma 4 (12B): An incredibly efficient, lightweight multimodal model built on the same architecture as Google's premier Gemini systems. It excels at reasoning, local agent tasks, and multimodal vision analysis on consumer hardware. [1, 2, 3]
  • Microsoft Phi-4 (3.8B / 14B): Known for its compact footprint and strong logic parsing, making it perfect for embedded software applications and fast, localized reasoning. [1, 2, 3]
  • Qwen 3.5 (0.8B to 9B): Highly flexible small-scale models from Alibaba that deliver outstanding multilingual support and function-calling utilities. [1]

🧠 Advanced Reasoning & General Chat Models

These models provide the best overall performance for daily conversations, deep thinking, mathematical analysis, and complex instruction-following. [1, 2]

  • DeepSeek-R1 (671B MoE / Quantized down to 1.5B–70B): DeepSeek's open-source reasoning powerhouse. It is highly celebrated for its step-by-step thinking processes, making it a favorite for complex problem-solving. [1, 2, 3, 4]
  • Meta Llama 4 Maverick / Scout: Meta's leading open model ecosystem featuring extended 10M token context windows, built intentionally to power sophisticated agent workflows and dense cross-document synthesis. [1, 2]
  • Qwen 3.8 / 3.6 (27B to 35B): Excellent "sweet spot" models that strike a balance between high accuracy and manageable hardware demands for self-hosting setups. [1, 2]

💻 Software Engineering & Agentic Coding Models

If you are looking to build applications, debug code, or implement autonomous developer agents, these models lead the pack. [1, 2]

  • Mistral Large 4 (1 Trillion params, MoE structure): A top-tier western open-weight model engineered specifically for cybersecurity defenses and autonomous agent software engineering.
  • Zhipu AI GLM-5.3 & GLM-5.3-Flash: Highly efficient code generation engines that dominate terminal execution and developer agent benchmarks globally.
  • Qwen 2.5 Coder (7B to 32B): A highly specialized, reliable series of code-specific engines optimized heavily for code repair, multi-file editing, and logical reasoning. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Summary Comparison Guide

![[Pasted image 20261029153924.png]]

Best Models for These Tasks

If you want to try this out right now using Ollama, I highly recommend downloading one of these two models:

  1. qwen2.5-coder:7b (Run: ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b): This is an absolute champion for writing scripts like PowerShell, Python, or Bash on normal laptops.
  2. gemma2:9b or llama3.1:8b: These are exceptionally articulate and perform beautifully for text editing, grammar fixing, and adjusting tone.

The Best Order to Install

  1. First, download and install Ollama
    • Ollama must be installed and running first so that it can hold and prepare the AI model engines.
    • Once installed, open your command prompt or terminal and run a model download command. For example, to download a fantastic all-around model, type: ollama run llama3.1 (or your chosen Qwen/Gemma model).
    • Test it with a quick message in the terminal to confirm it works, then close the terminal. Ollama will keep running silently in your system tray.
  2. Second, download and install AnythingLLM Desktop
    • Install the desktop application.
    • When you launch AnythingLLM for the first time, it will walk you through a setup wizard and ask: "Which LLM provider would you like to use?"
    • Select Ollama from the list. Because Ollama is already running on your machine, AnythingLLM will automatically detect it and instantly display a list of all the models you downloaded in Step 1.

⚙️ How They Run Side-by-Side

Once configured, they live in perfect harmony on your computer:

  • Zero Connection Effort: Every time you open AnythingLLM in the future, it automatically talks to Ollama in the background. You don't need to manually configure any complicated network addresses.
  • The Workflow: You will use AnythingLLM's window to create workspaces, click a button to upload your private files, and chat with the AI. Behind the scenes, AnythingLLM safely sends the text over to Ollama to process the data entirely on your graphics card or RAM.

docs.title: Gemma4 README
docs.text:
Hugging Face | GitHub | Launch Blog | Documentation License: Apache 2.0 | Authors: Google DeepMind

[!Note] This model card is for the Gemma 4 12B Unified model, which is part of the Gemma 4 family of open models. Built with the same multimodal functionality as Gemma 4 E2B and E4B (text, audio, image, and video inputs), it brings native audio and vision understanding directly to local environments without the need for separate encoders. This unified approach to multimodality makes the model encoder-free, offering a deployment size that is perfect for consumer devices and streamlined local execution.

Gemma is a family of open models built by Google DeepMind. Gemma 4 models are multimodal, handling text and image input (with audio supported on E2B, E4B, and 12B) and generating text output. This release includes open-weights models in both pre-trained and instruction-tuned variants. Gemma 4 features a context window of up to 256K tokens and maintains multilingual support in over 140 languages.

Featuring both Dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, Gemma 4 is well-suited for tasks like text generation, coding, and reasoning. The models are available in five distinct sizes: E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B, and 31B. Their diverse sizes make them deployable in environments ranging from high-end phones to laptops and servers, democratizing access to state-of-the-art AI.

Gemma 4 introduces key capability and architectural advancements:

  • Reasoning â€“ All models in the family are designed as highly capable reasoners, with configurable thinking modes.

  • Extended Multimodalities â€“ Processes Text, Image with variable aspect ratio and resolution support (all models), Video, and Audio (featured natively on the E2B, E4B, and 12B models).

  • Diverse & Efficient Architectures â€“ Offers Dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants of different sizes for scalable deployment.

  • Optimized for On-Device â€“ Smaller models are specifically designed for efficient local execution on laptops and mobile devices.

  • Increased Context Window â€“ The small models feature a 128K context window, while the medium models support 256K.

  • Enhanced Coding & Agentic Capabilities â€“ Achieves notable improvements in coding benchmarks alongside native function-calling support, powering highly capable autonomous agents.

  • Native System Prompt Support â€“ Gemma 4 introduces native support for the system role, enabling more structured and controllable conversations.

docs.title: Models Overview
docs.text:
Gemma 4 models are designed to deliver frontier-level performance at each size, targeting deployment scenarios from mobile and edge devices (E2B, E4B) to consumer GPUs and workstations (12B, 26B A4B, 31B). They are well-suited for reasoning, agentic workflows, coding, and multimodal understanding.

The models employ a hybrid attention mechanism that interleaves local sliding window attention with full global attention, ensuring the final layer is always global. This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks. To optimize memory for long contexts, global layers feature unified Keys and Values, and apply Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE).

docs.title: Dense Models
docs.text:
Property E2B E4B 12B Unified 31B Dense Total Parameters 2.3B effective (5.1B with embeddings) 4.5B effective (8B with embeddings) 11.95B 30.7B Layers 35 42 48 60 Sliding Window 512 tokens 512 tokens 1024 tokens 1024 tokens Context Length 128K tokens 128K tokens 256K tokens 256K tokens Vocabulary Size 262K 262K 262K 262K Supported Modalities Text, Image, Audio Text, Image, Audio Text, Image, Audio Text, Image Vision Encoder Parameters ~150M ~150M - ~550M Audio Encoder Parameters ~300M ~300M - No Audio

The "E" in E2B and E4B stands for "effective" parameters. The smaller models incorporate Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE) to maximize parameter efficiency in on-device deployments. Rather than adding more layers or parameters to the model, PLE gives each decoder layer its own small embedding for every token. These embedding tables are large but are only used for quick lookups, which is why the effective parameter count is much smaller than the total.

The "Unified" in Gemma 4 12B Unified refers to its encoder-free architecture. Other Gemma 4 models use dedicated encoders to process multimodal data before passing it to the LLM. Gemma 4 12B eliminates these encoders entirely, projecting raw image patches and audio waveforms directly into the LLM's embedding space through lightweight linear layers. This unified approach means all modalities flow straight into a single decoder-only transformer, reducing multimodal latency and allowing the entire model to be fine-tuned in one pass.

docs.title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Model
docs.text:
Property 26B A4B MoE Total Parameters 25.2B Active Parameters 3.8B Layers 30 Sliding Window 1024 tokens Context Length 256K tokens Vocabulary Size 262K Expert Count 8 active / 128 total and 1 shared Supported Modalities Text, Image Vision Encoder Parameters ~550M

The "A" in 26B A4B stands for "active parameters" in contrast to the total number of parameters the model contains. By only activating a 4B subset of parameters during inference, the Mixture-of-Experts model runs much faster than its 26B total might suggest. This makes it an excellent choice for fast inference compared to the dense 31B model since it runs almost as fast as a 4B-parameter model.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
Gemma 4 models handle a broad range of tasks across text, vision, and audio. Key capabilities include:

  • Thinking â€“ Built-in reasoning mode that lets the model think step-by-step before answering.
  • Long Context â€“ Context windows of up to 128K tokens (E2B/E4B) and 256K tokens (12B, 26B A4B/31B).
  • Image Understanding â€“ Object detection, Document/PDF parsing, screen and UI understanding, chart comprehension, OCR (including multilingual), handwriting recognition, and pointing. Images can be processed at variable aspect ratios and resolutions.
  • Video Understanding â€“ Analyze video by processing sequences of frames.
  • Interleaved Multimodal Input â€“ Freely mix text and images in any order within a single prompt.
  • Function Calling â€“ Native support for structured tool use, enabling agentic workflows.
  • Coding â€“ Code generation, completion, and correction.
  • Multilingual â€“ Out-of-the-box support for 35+ languages, pre-trained on 140+ languages.
  • Audio (E2B, E4B, and 12B only) â€“ Automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech-to-translated-text translation across multiple languages.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
You can use all Gemma 4 models with the latest version of Transformers. To get started, install the necessary dependencies in your environment:

pip install -U transformers torch accelerate

Once you have everything installed, you can proceed to load the model with the code below:

from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM

MODEL_ID = "google/gemma-4-12B-it"

# Load model
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    dtype="auto",
    device_map="auto"
)

Once the model is loaded, you can start generating output:

# Prompt
messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a short joke about saving RAM."},
]

# Process input
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=True,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=False
).to(model.device)
input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]

# Generate output
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024)
response = processor.decode(outputs[0][input_len:], skip_special_tokens=False)

# Parse output
processor.parse_response(response)

To enable reasoning, set enable_thinking=True and the parse_response function will take care of parsing the thinking output.

Below, you will also find snippets for processing audio (E2B, E4B, 12B only), images, and video alongside text:
